content: Need help tuning SQL queries for CTFs? I can show you some neat tricks.
Yeah, I'm trying to bypass some input validation. Looking to chop off the rest of the query after my payload.

Classic! You can end your injection with double-dash: 
' OR 1=1 --
That cuts off anything after your code.
Nice. Is there a way to do it without the double-dash? Maybe something shorter?

Absolutely: MySQL lets you use # for comments. Try: 
' OR 1=1 #
Everything after # is ignored.
What if the filter blocks both -- and #? Any other ways to kill the rest?

You can use C-style block comments:
' OR 1=1 /*
This buries trailing code, so the original query gets cut off.
Will /* always work or are there quirks I should know?
With /*, you need to make sure you don't close the comment unless you want to resume code. You can also nest them for more stealth: /* /* */
I've seen --+ used before. What's the + for?

--+ is a trick: some filters only look for --. The '+' is treated as whitespace, so:
' OR 1=1 --+ 
acts like a comment start.
Do spaces matter after these comment markers?

Yes, SQL expects a space after -- before the comment. --something won't work, but -- something will. --+ or --
 are both valid.
Can you bury an injection mid-query with comments? Like splitting up a payload?

Definitely. Try:
UNION/**/SELECT/**/password/**/FROM/**/users
Comments break up keywords and can evade naive filters.
Awesome, thanks. How about combining these for extra stealth?

Sure: 
' OR/**/1=1--+
This combines obfuscated spacing and comment markers to slip past most basic filters.
